approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted, task-local observations. It retains a greedy population of 64 scored molecules, samples breeding parents across high-score quantiles, and builds a fresh field with connected-fragment crossover, finishing mutations and ordinary mutation continuation. Stable canonical identity and duplicate checks admit valid graphs; a narrow sulfur rule rejects newly introduced outside-envelope signatures relative to the maximum multiplicity in the actual scored generating parents. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. A Gaussian process fitted to the complete accepted archive uses chirality-aware radius-two Morgan counts and a count-Tanimoto kernel, with the current raw-score mean and population standard deviation. It selects ten distinct offspring from 160 by successive masked maxima of correlated posterior function draws, then learns and breeds from real accepted feedback.
approach.novelty: Add a bounded DPP-Thompson batch sampler that treats the whole batch as one selection decision. Begin with the Parent's original batch and propose slot replacements using fresh maxima of the same correlated posterior over the entire pool. A covariance determinant reweights acceptance toward batches that offer complementary modeled information, while posterior-maximizer proposals retain a quality preference. Run a fixed twenty attempts per announced batch member. This differs from siblings that changed field width, predictive features, the allocation mean or residual dependence, and from earlier fantasy projection, a variance-only final slot and greedy incumbent utility. Its new contribution is determinant-based coupling of the unchanged quality proposals; productive exploration and endpoint benefit remain hypotheses.

observed_bottleneck: The limiting behavior is insufficient productive exploration in the learned fresh field, with redundant batches and weak conversion of local selection into reliable absolute endpoint progress. The actual n-1744a1494180 seed-0/1/2 summary.json and run.log files are complete: fifteen successful cells, 300 calls per task, ten-member batches, no invalid or duplicate emissions, macro mean 0.59645311428869 and population SD 0.03397032998399878. A read-only recount of all fifteen published candidate logs finds 435 batches and 4350 accepted offspring, only 648 strict best-generating-parent beats (0.1489655172413793), 255 sequential incumbent updates, mean offspring score 0.372049560842182 versus mean best-generating-parent score 0.4553040448335957, and mean within-batch count-Tanimoto similarity 0.6727889890385363. This describes the actual Parent stream, not a causal diagnosis of redundancy. Its own-parent mean gain was only +0.0007834645552323346, with seed deltas +0.017686193676039963, +0.002307179813052951 and -0.01764297982339591. In n-da0eeecfb462, widening the same field raised its best available modeled quality but not selected enrichment (1.043 versus 1.054 pool-SD units); the full endpoint delta was -0.016060, dominated by the inherited deco_hop seed-0 breakthrough. Current mean-only n-f04cec6ab705 and correlation-removal n-8df0bb3bbcfe instead lost 0.11631688199011732 and 0.05054466462284635 despite more local parent wins. On the different, ungated code Parent, variance-only n-062b351ccb52 lost 0.022789878982636996: none of its final-position molecules beat its generating parent, advanced the incumbent or later bred. Incumbent-targeted n-8a62df15e51f raised sampled utility but lost 0.05627557001043134. These controls argue for retaining correlated quality proposals while testing a distinct whole-batch coupling rule; they do not establish that diversity will help or identify a mediator.

literature_review.conclusion: A real search and primary-paper/reference-code inspection support adapting DPP-TS's posterior-maximizer proposal plus determinant-reweighting mechanism. Retain the current correlated count-GP and fresh generator because current mean-only and covariance-removal controls lost; register a new acquisition principle within the existing posterior-allocation family. Use only the ticket's fixed distinct-support 20B chain, inherited initialization, original full-pool proposal law, C_plus determinant and noise value. The chosen work bound is new engineering, with no literature claim of mixing, optimality or reliable gain. Reject pure-variance, hallucinated-mean projection, greedy incumbent utility, lambda/cutoff variants and all parameter rescue for this ticket.

sources.applicability: Adopt this quality-proposal-plus-determinant principle at the Parent's full finite-pool boundary. Distinct-identity self transitions, actual sampled jittered covariance and exactly 20B attempts are declared benchmark adaptations. Adaptive pools, model misspecification and deterministic scores give neither certified mixing nor inherited regret guarantees. The publication was also checked at https://proceedings.mlr.press/v151/nava22a.html.
sources.finding: The paper reweights posterior-maximizer batches by det(I+sigma^-2 K_S). Algorithm 1 chooses a uniform replacement position, proposes an independent posterior maximizer and accepts using the determinant ratio; Appendix A.1 explains cancellation of the intractable maximizer probabilities. Its sampler runs to convergence and its regret analysis assumes a GP-generated objective.
sources.title: Nava, Mutny and Krause (AISTATS 2022): Diversified Sampling for Batched Bayesian Optimization with Determinantal Point Processes, sections 4.2-4.3, Algorithm 1 and Appendix A.1

sources.applicability: Use as primary implementation corroboration only. Its optional lambda/cutoff/first-TS settings and duplicate-permitting initialization are not the frozen recipe. Write the small finite-pool sampler with existing torch operations, preserving the Parent's source/runtime boundary; do not vendor its GP/true-function evaluation harness or add assets/dependencies.
sources.finding: The repository README credits the paper authors for this release. The snippet calls an inherited posterior sample-point operation, uniformly swaps a batch position, uses I+noise^-2 posterior covariance and a determinant acceptance ratio, and decrements n_runs for every attempt. Its header states intended CC BY 4.0 attribution.
sources.title: Author-provided DPP-TS snippet released in the SOBER benchmark repository, pinned commit 3cd4449a249294e0a8b9261bb32afde23ed8341c

hypothesis: Replace only full-pool batch allocation with distinct-support finite-pool DPP-TS: initialize with the inherited masked correlated Thompson batch, form L=I+(F F^T)/(0.05^2) from its actual standardized jittered Cholesky factor F, and execute exactly 20B uniform-position Metropolis proposals from fresh unmasked full-pool correlated posterior maximizers, taking duplicate self transitions and accepting other replacements by the determinant ratio while preserving slot order.

finding_summary.headline: Determinant repulsion diversifies batches but lowers predicted quality and the complete endpoint mean
finding_summary.insights: The determinant acceptance rule measurably adds separation beyond simply refreshing posterior-maximizer proposals. Replaying the same saved proposals while accepting every valid replacement gives count similarity 0.6540, log determinant 39.6516 and mean enrichment 0.9552, compared with the actual sampler’s 0.5798, 41.8934 and 0.7287. That is a local geometry and predicted-quality tradeoff; those passive alternatives have no observed labels or descendants. Broader productive cores did not supply larger total progress: newly productive typed-core descendants had more incumbent advances but less cumulative gain, while the corresponding generic-core cohort improved, so reuse is mixed rather than absent. The chemistry assessment also finds low-scoring tiny fragments and questionable closures alongside useful aromatic, carbonyl and amine context; fingerprint separation does not establish better functional relationships or feasibility. This fixed recipe activates its intended diversification but fails the performance hypothesis and ends without parameter rescue. Mixing error, true information gain, regret and the chemical or ancestry mediator of the endpoint loss remain unmeasured; this result does not settle other allocation methods or the retained foundation’s contribution.
finding_summary.results: All 435 finite chains completed their 200 attempts, and every transition reconstructed. On the same actual candidate pools, average count similarity fell from 0.6660 to 0.5798 and modeled batch log determinant rose from 39.2105 to 41.8934. The effect was aggregate: 83 batches became more similar and 53 finished with a lower determinant. Predicted mean enrichment fell from 0.9888 to 0.7287 pool standard deviations while latent uncertainty rose. Original predictions stayed identical on every emitted identity. More parent-beating cores appeared and entered later breeding, but absolute offspring scores fell from the Parent’s 0.3720 to 0.3353, and total sequential incumbent gain fell from 5.8194 to 5.2470. The complete fifteen-cell endpoint mean was 0.558294 versus 0.596453, a change of −0.038159; all three seed means fell and twelve endpoints lost. The Parent’s late deco_hop breakthrough stays in this primary result. The descriptive other-fourteen-cell mean change is also negative, −0.023254.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic and amine families retain labile heteroatom bonds, difficult closures and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: All supplied Child and published Parent trajectories were present and read: five tasks, Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, 300 observations per session, with 900 records and 870 optimizer observations per task. No task lacks trajectories and no requested comparison path is missing. context.comparison reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true against code Parent n-1744a1494180, with no profile-mismatched seeds. These are complete descriptive chemical comparisons of adaptively diverging streams, not common later candidate pools or component attribution. The output includes substituted indole amides and ketones, linked nitrogen-rich carbonyl/thione heterocycles, aryl-containing cyclic and secondary amines, quinoline-linked nitrogen-carbonyl rings, and fluorinated imino/carbonyl polycycles. Ring-closure-string incidences range from 0.9345 to 0.9644; aromatic-string incidences range from 0.6977 to 0.9414. These counters report molecular incidences of text features, not perceived ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. All stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0; charge-string incidence is 0.0011 for zaleplon_mpo and 0.0 elsewhere. Neutral notation nevertheless includes clearly protonatable aliphatic amines. Recognizable medicinal-chemistry fragments coexist with N-halogen and O-F bonds, constrained unsaturation and densely connected rings. Some scaffolds appear makeable, but these liabilities also occur among leaders, supporting questionable synthetic plausibility and weak overall drug-likeness. Different seeds and tasks reach distinct families; leading chemistry within a seed is much narrower, so structural diversity is moderate rather than globally collapsed. Digest final_molecules are late seed-2 proposals, not all seed incumbents. Scores below are recorded labels and their structural associations; they do not certify synthesis, stability, stereochemical preference or biological activity. Historical gap provenance was read through the evidence_index in the published reports of n-c55c3d520a2c (Development), n-62daf219c70a (same-code profile baseline) and n-1744a1494180. The baseline report explicitly describes exact historical trajectory reproduction with a profile-mismatched comparison; that history is not pooled as independent replication of the present current-profile panel.

per_task.generated_character: Medium-sized, mostly aromatic molecules retain an indole-like region linked to an aryl or azaaryl carbonyl group, with methyl, vinyl, methoxy, thiol or methylthio substitution. Seed 2 favors an N-chloro anilide; seed 0 develops more connected aza/ether rings carrying a pyridyl amide; seed 1 retains an indole ketone linked through methylene to an azaaryl ring. The optimizer mean SMILES length is 41.0, ring-string incidence 0.9379 and aromatic-string incidence 0.9276. Indole, amide and aryl-ketone chemistry is recognizable, but N-halogen attachments, imines and some connected-ring variants make feasibility uneven. Parent leaders also retain indole/azaindole-carbonyl families, including an N-hydroxy amide and an adjacent thiocarbonyl/carbonyl link; the Child has not eliminated their broader local-reactivity and geometry concerns.
liabilities: The leading seed-2 amide has an N-Cl bond; other strong variants include ring N-Br, imine and enamine-like attachments.
Dense connected rings and altered unsaturation require geometric assessment beyond valence-valid SMILES.
Late ethene and disulfane observations and very large aromatic concatenations lose the useful chemical context.
missing_features: Consistent conventional amide and substituent alternatives preserving the compact aromatic/carbonyl organization; high labels still coexist with labile N-halogen attachments.
Chemically independent plausible scaffold alternatives are poorly represented among leaders within a seed, despite abundant aromatic rings.
Explicit stereochemical identity is absent where saturated connected-ring variants introduce potentially stereogenic environments; the trajectory does not establish a stereochemical score penalty.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145. The seed-2 vinyl/methyl/methoxy N-chloro indole anilide reaches 0.4484138510190879 at evaluation 224; the seed-0 connected pyridyl-amide leader reaches 0.4338406416200045 and the seed-1 indole/azaaryl ketone 0.42348216717712805. These support compact organized aromatic/carbonyl context, not a universal requirement for N-Cl. A late enlarged unsaturated ring/dicarbonyl relative scores 0.12984982838027212, whereas the nearby indole/pyridyl-amide proposal scores 0.43643070309403553. An early doubled indole/anilide proposal scores 1.2911590938020179e-12; C=C and SS score 0.0 even late in the runs. Extra aromatic material and complete fragmentation both fail to replace the useful molecular arrangement. Parent seed endpoints are 0.4593573492521118, 0.47411701813450596 and 0.4369542269692598, with different local substitutions; this does not isolate any individual bond effect.

per_task.generated_character: This is the largest and most elaborate output by mean SMILES length, 69.3, with maximum length 204; ring-string incidence is 0.9448 and aromatic-string incidence 0.9414. Seed 1 combines a nitrogen-rich carbonyl/thione fused system with an azaaryl region through an aminomethyl link, with ethyl/methyl, fluorovinyl and O-F groups. Seed 2 favors linked, densely fused azaaromatic and dicarbonyl rings with carbon-bound fluorine or bromine. Seed 0 instead extends the heterocyclic motifs with long conjugated, brominated and imine-rich regions. Familiar heterocyclic fragments are present, but O-F attachments, unusual fusion patterns and ring-constrained cumulenes weaken synthetic plausibility. Parent output reaches a compact linked carbonyl/thione-azaaryl family in seed 0, a cyanate/S-Br-bearing family in seed 1 and a nitroso/small-ring family in seed 2; both streams retain substantial liabilities.
liabilities: O-F bonds occur in the highest-scoring seed-1 family; conventional thiones and thioethers should be distinguished from these separate local liabilities.
The cyclic cumulated-double-bond relative and densely fused azaaromatic graphs need ring-size and geometric assessment.
Seed-0 leaders carry extensive brominated unsaturation and imine-rich elaboration, while a late F entry remains a floor-scoring observation.
missing_features: Reliable access to compact alternative connections of the retained azaaryl and carbonyl/thione regions; one Child seed elaborates long conjugated appendages instead.
Geometrically credible saturated and unsaturated ring alternatives are not consistently distinguished, even where their labels are exactly tied.
Stable local alternatives to O-F and highly reactive peripheral groups are not consistently represented among leaders; their causal score benefit remains unmeasured.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl fused dione scores 0.548381482770623; the entries F, FF and small nonaromatic reagents sit at 0.5. Child seed endpoints are 0.6093137254901961, 0.6155197150348786 and 0.614198334200937. The higher labels associate with complete nitrogen-rich heterocyclic arrangements. In seed 2, shortening the saturated ring segment from CCC to CC leaves the score exactly 0.614198334200937. The related brominated structures with saturated, alkenyl or cyclic cumulated segments all score 0.6134784622510421. This visible plateau does not establish a reward for more mass or difficult unsaturation. The published Parent seed-0 breakthrough at evaluation 281 scores 0.8561477222467935 and is a separate inherited realization, while this Child seed-0 long-chain leader stays at 0.6093137254901961. Parent seed-1 and seed-2 endpoints are 0.6204376881838878 and 0.6442339647723496. The chemistry comparison points to different complete connectivities, not a measured benefit of any single substituent or selector component.

per_task.generated_character: The leaders are medium-sized aryl-containing basic amines, not nitrogen-poor fragments. Seed 0 combines a phenolic ethylaryl region, a methylamino-bearing linker and a cyclic aryl amine with a very small O-containing closure across adjacent aromatic atoms. Seed 1 favors chlorinated aryl regions, aniline substitution and a cyclic aminoether region with a brominated unsaturated appendage. Seed 2 has N-methylpyrrolidine linked through a secondary amine to a phenolic, fluorinated aryl-bearing cyclopropyl region. Mean SMILES length is 58.4; ring-string incidence is 0.9483, aromatic-string incidence 0.9287 and halogen-string incidence 0.9575. Recognizable amines and ordinary carbon-bound halogens coexist with difficult ring closures and unspecified configurations. Parent leaders also present cyclic basic amines with aryl surfaces, including a relatively recognizable diaryl diaza-ring thioether in seed 1.
liabilities: A highest-scoring molecule still contains a very small O-containing ring spanning adjacent aromatic atoms; its label is not a geometry certificate.
Other leaders retain brominated unsaturation and enamine-like groups, requiring environment-specific stability assessment.
Potentially stereogenic saturated and bridged structures have no explicit stereochemical notation; N-N linkage variants add a separate local liability.
missing_features: Explicit stereochemical control around aryl-bearing saturated linkers, substituted cyclopropyl regions and connected rings; basic amine centres themselves are already present.
Consistently credible ring geometry alongside the learned aryl/amine arrangement, particularly alternatives to the very small aromatic O-containing closures.
Defined protonation and tautomeric interpretation for the available amines and imines is not demonstrated; the trajectory establishes no benefit for introducing formal charges.

Child seed leaders reach 0.9894589357328201, 0.9691235861880112 and 0.9852408074527423. The strongest visible association is the arrangement of available aliphatic amine centres with aromatic surface; nitrogen count or ring presence alone does not explain the contrast. The seed-2 N-methylpyrrolidine/secondary-amine family already scores 0.9766075530428495 with an imine-bearing side chain and 0.9852408074527423 with fluoromethyl substitution. Its final hydroxymethyl relative scores 0.9671682064542053, while a changed N-N-linked relative scores 0.7299797110507354. Neutral SMILES does not show absence of basic centres, and these labels do not determine solution protonation or actual affinity.

per_task.generated_character: Medium-to-large nitrogen-carbonyl ring systems dominate, with comparatively little halogen chemistry: mean SMILES length 51.6, ring-string incidence 0.9644, aromatic-string incidence 0.9414 and halogen-string incidence 0.1057. Seed 2 links a methylquinoline region through a benzylic aryl ether to densely connected N-methyl amine, amide and ketone rings. Seed 0 keeps a phenyl/azaheterocycle-carbonyl region joined to an alkoxy-substituted partially unsaturated ring; seed 1 develops a fused aromatic nitrogen framework with lactam and N-methyl carbonyl-ring functionality. Conventional quinoline, ether and amide fragments make some output recognizable, although fusion, bridging and late N-N/S-N extensions complicate synthesis. Parent leaders also combine azaaryl/quinoline and nitrogen-dicarbonyl regions, with different ring connections and shorter local variants.
liabilities: Dense fused and bridged carbonyl/amine rings create geometric and synthetic questions even in halogen-free leaders.
Late cyclic cumulated segments, S-N connections and N-N-N-containing extensions differ substantially from ordinary lactams in local feasibility.
The output continues to admit small isolated reagents at zero score and incompletely specified saturated-ring configurations.
missing_features: Consistently accessible alternative connections of azaaryl and nitrogen-carbonyl regions, preserving their combined context without automatically increasing bridge complexity.
Explicit stereochemical identity and conformationally credible saturated-ring connections where dense bridges are generated.
Independent plausible scaffold alternatives remain limited within each leading series; numerous unique strings are insufficient evidence of such coverage.

per_task.generated_character: Compact-to-medium fluorinated, nitrogen-rich imino/carbonyl polycycles dominate the stronger output, with mean SMILES length 53.3, ring-string incidence 0.9345, aromatic-string incidence 0.6977 and halogen-string incidence 0.8586. Parent leaders are also fluorinated imino/carbonyl heterocycles; their higher labels in some seeds do not imply conventional synthesis.

The seed-1 cyclic cumulene and strongly connected small rings raise substantial geometric and synthetic questions.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Origin: n-c55c3d520a2c Development output; carried through the same-code profile baseline n-62daf219c70a and the published n-1744a1494180 report. Re-observed in n-9b90d71cc6e1 versus n-1744a1494180 on the complete current-profile Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, with 300 observations per session and batch 10. A leading indole anilide contains N-Cl, a linked carbonyl/thione family contains O-F, and fluorinated imino/carbonyl leaders retain N-F. In one observed paired local family, a carbon-fluorinated sulfur-ring structure scores 0.5720686252952984 and its O-F-bearing relative 0.5163374846626305. Useful ordinary carbon-bound halogens, amines, thiones and thioethers also occur; the gap is environment-dependent, not their wholesale absence. The inherited narrow sulfur condition does not certify these other environments.
transferable_gaps.gap: Conventional local bond environments are not consistently retained when useful aromatic and heterocyclic frameworks are modified.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide bond-environment-aware transformations and conventional local alternatives preserving favorable functional relationships learned only from the current session. Preserve useful amines and ordinary carbon-bound halogens and distinguish conventional sulfur chemistry from other attachments. These conditional output associations neither identify a responsible component nor establish that a blanket filter or universal replacement improves the endpoint.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Origin: n-c55c3d520a2c Development ring-geometry gap, reproduced by n-62daf219c70a and carried by n-1744a1494180. Current evidence is n-9b90d71cc6e1 versus its published Parent n-1744a1494180, Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, 300 observations per session and batch 10 under the supplied matched profile. A high-labelled aryl/cyclic-amine leader has a very small O-containing closure across adjacent aromatic atoms. Other families contain small cyclic cumulenes or densely connected unsaturated rings. A saturated, an alkenyl and a cyclic cumulated relative share the exact label 0.6134784622510421; string variation and this label do not assess geometry. Conventional saturated cyclic amines also occur at strong labels, and ring-string incidence is high, so ring formation itself is not missing.
transferable_gaps.gap: Representable ring graphs are not consistently distinguished from geometrically credible unsaturation and connected-ring topology.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make ring edits sensitive to ring size, unsaturation geometry and bridge connectivity, while offering feasible alternative topologies that retain learned functional arrangements. Distinguish ordinary small and fused rings from doubtful closures. This is a conditional chemical-feasibility gap; it attributes no motif to a specific component and establishes no benefit from forbidding ring chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Origin: n-c55c3d520a2c Development stereochemical-identity gap, retained by the same-code n-62daf219c70a baseline and n-1744a1494180. Re-observed in the complete current-profile n-9b90d71cc6e1 versus n-1744a1494180 Search panel, seeds 0, 1 and 2, 300 observations per session and batch 10. Every Child digest stereocentre-string incidence is 0.0, and the full Child trajectories contain no explicit tetrahedral or directional alkene stereo notation. Aryl-bearing saturated amine linkers, substituted cyclopropyl regions, fluorinated ring centres and dense bridges visibly create environments where stereochemical identity needs assessment. Some aromatic leaders can be achiral. Neutral records contain basic amines, so charge markers cannot be used as a proxy for missing nitrogen chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: Potentially stereogenic and configuration-dependent molecular arrangements remain incompletely specified after generation.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve or deliberately resolve stereochemistry when chemically meaningful, including configuration after ring reconnection and substituted-alkene edits, with separate treatment of achiral and configurationally unstable cases. Interpret protonation and tautomerism independently. This evidence shows unspecified identity; it proves neither a stereochemical score penalty nor component attribution.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Origin: n-c55c3d520a2c Development context-retention gap; same-code reproduction in n-62daf219c70a and continued evidence in n-1744a1494180. Present evidence is the complete matched-profile n-9b90d71cc6e1/Parent n-1744a1494180 Search panel, seeds 0, 1 and 2, 300 observations per session and batch 10. Late ethene, disulfane, halogen-only and fluorosulfur fragments reach observed floors or near-zero labels. Large doubled aromatic systems also have extremely small labels, while stronger molecules retain combined aromatic, carbonyl, heterocyclic or amine regions. Conversely, shortening a saturated segment leaves one label exactly 0.614198334200937, showing that meaningful simplification is already possible and size alone is not the relevant property.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful functional-group context is inconsistently preserved when molecules are fragmented, enlarged or reconnected.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use current-session accepted feedback to preserve useful combinations of chemical regions during shrinking, growth and reconnection, while allowing genuine simplification and productive elaboration. A fixed minimum size or preference for more aromatic mass does not follow. The observed labels describe context loss and redundancy without assigning the cause to a graph operator or selector.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Origin: n-c55c3d520a2c Development leading-family coverage gap, preserved through n-62daf219c70a and n-1744a1494180. Re-observed for n-9b90d71cc6e1 versus n-1744a1494180 on complete current-profile Search seeds 0, 1 and 2 at 300 observations per session and batch 10. Leading series repeatedly change short chains, halogen position, imine/carbonyl attachments or nearby ring segments on retained indole, linked azaheterocycle, aryl-amine and nitrogen-dicarbonyl frameworks. Different seeds do reach different families and recognizable alternatives occur, so the evidence supports limited plausible local alternatives rather than global scaffold collapse. The historical baseline is reproduction rather than independent chemical replication; its labels are not pooled here.
transferable_gaps.gap: Chemically independent plausible alternatives to a leading scaffold family are not consistently represented within a seed.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer independent, feasible connectivities that preserve favorable functional-group relationships learned from current-session observations. method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
